proposals.title: Score engine: a Math estimate that moves with every answer, and the points still on the table
proposals.what:
SERVER (F4, server/estimate.py): new estimate.practice(learner, tz). Inputs: clean first-try answers from the last 60 days. Repeats, disputed and voided answers are left out; a guess counts 0.5 (R8). For each (topic, tier, format) keep a Beta posterior. Its prior is the field's first-try rate on that (topic, tier) once n>=50; before that it is the stated defaults (easy 0.80, medium 0.55, hard 0.30), with weight 4. Answers older than 21 days weigh 0.5.

SIMULATION: blueprint.slots('module1',1) gives the 22 (domain, tier, format) slots. A slot's topic mix is the share of that domain's (template, tier) abilities (blueprint.abilities()), the way blueprint.fill draws them. Run an exact Poisson-binomial over module 1 for P(route up), using route_after at 60%. Then take expected earned points on each module-2 route and pass them through scoring.section_score, so the practice estimate and the test bands sit on one scale by construction. The band comes from 1,000 Monte-Carlo sittings. Cache per learner and recompute after every 10 attempts or on a new local day.

GATE: needs 150 clean answers covering at least 12 of 19 skills. Until then it shows 'Estimate after 150 answers in 12 skills · 82 answers, 9 skills so far' with a meter and a 'Fill the gaps' button (one question in each uncovered skill).

POINTS ON THE TABLE: for each skill, re-run with that skill lifted to max(p, 0.85) at every tier. The gain in the median is that skill's points. Rank by points per estimated minute, where minutes = questions needed to move the posterior times the student's median time. Output gains=[{topic, points, now:'54% on medium', share:'15% of the section', minutes}]. Each open trap also gets its expected points lost per section: P(its template fills a slot) x P(miss) x slot value.

ROUTING LINE: 'Upper module 2 in 62% of simulated sittings. 2 more right in module 1 lifts the 580 ceiling; easy and medium Algebra is the cheapest way there.'

SCREENS:
- Today score card, second row: 'From practice 600-660 · +20 since Monday · 1,240 answers', plus 'Where your next points are' (top 3, each with Practise).
- Results overview: the practice estimate as a dotted band between test bars, and a full 19-row Points table (points, accuracy by tier, share of the section, Practise).
- Tests estimate card: both numbers, with 'Tests win when they disagree'.
- Plan: the SplitBar is labelled in points.

HONESTY: always labelled 'from practice' and never replaces a test band. A new table estimate_log(learner, session, mid, low, high, at) stores the prediction at each finished section. The report shows 'Practice said 630 · this section 610-690'. Help shows the mean error once 20 or more pairs exist.

STUDENT DOES DIFFERENTLY: spends the next hour on the skill worth the most points (usually easy and medium questions in the 35% domains, and whatever is below the routing cut), not on their favourite or hardest topic, and sees the number move each week. WHY IT MOVES THE SCORE: time goes where the marginal points are, and visible progress between tests keeps practice going.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep gives an estimate only after a test: Score Overview stays empty until all four modules are done. It drops floor-score sections and shows a red LOW CONFIDENCE with no way to raise it. Their plan weights 'weak areas' the student picks by domain, and their domain cards read '20% of test section, 1-5 questions'. No screen of theirs puts a point value on anything. Ours updates from every answer, shows how routing caps the score, and ranks skills by points per minute. That needs difficulty- and skill-tagged answers at volume, which only our bank produces.
proposals.needs: F4 estimate.py (practice(), gains(), estimate_log table added to §2.5), scoring.section_score and route_after, blueprint.slots/abilities (S5 owns blueprint.py after wave 1), R8 clean-answer columns, S4 per-type crowd rates as priors. Consumers: S3 (score card, Up next reason), S6 (Results band and Points table, report line), S5 (estimate card), S7 (SplitBar labels, drift), F2 (shell Today card). Prior defaults and the 150/12 gate go into open question 12.

proposals.title: One 'What next' engine behind every page, with the reason and the payoff
proposals.what:
SERVER: server/next.py, GET /api/next?from=today|summary|report|review|shell&sid=. It returns an ordered list of [{kind, title, minutes, reason, payoff, action: href or a drill body, pinned}].

HARD RULES FIRST (Today §3a rules 1-2 today): a running timed test, then an unfinished set.

SCORED CANDIDATES:
- today's plan tasks (S7 plan.today_summary)
- fixed-mistake check-ins due (R9)
- due question types (proposal 4)
- open traps
- the week's test
- words due (S9)
- the day's questions and the challenge (S3, S8)
- 'Fix these N' from the sitting just finished

SCORE: expected points gained per minute (from the score engine; a check-in is worth its trap's points x the relapse risk; words are a small constant) x urgency (days overdue, a running clock, fewer than 3 hours left in the local day). The sum is capped by today's minutes left against the goal. Each item carries a reason line built from the numbers ('4 check-ins due · a missed one reopens a fixed mistake') and a payoff ('keeps ~6 points').

CONSUMERS:
- Today Up next: item 1 is the big card; items 2-4 head the Today list.
- Practice summary NextActions: 'Next: 4 check-ins due · 5 min [Start]', with 'Or: Fix my 3 misses' beside it.
- Report: ends with the same.
- Review header: 'Next: 6 due · 8 min'.
- Shell Today card: 'Next: Circles check-in'.
- Palette: 'What should I do now?'
- Goal already met: 'Today's goal done. Optional: 10 more in Circles, about +4 points.'

Every 'next' on the site comes from this one call, so no two pages can disagree.

STUDENT DOES DIFFERENTLY: never has to decide what to study; after any activity the best next one is one tap away and says why. WHY IT MOVES THE SCORE: sessions end at 'what now?', and ordering by points per minute gets more score out of each hour studied.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep's dashboard has no single next action (the plan CTA, QOTD, countdown and score all compete), and a QBank session ends with Next disabled on the last question, no summary and nowhere to go. The v2 spec has four separate next rules that can disagree: Today §3a, the session NextActions, Plan tasks, and Review's 'Check these now'.
proposals.needs: Score engine (proposal 1) for points; S7 plan.today_summary; R9 check-ins; proposal 4's due types; S9 words.today_summary; S8 challenge state; S3 QOTD state. A new §2.9 contract line. Consumers: S3 Up next, S4 summary, S6 report, S10 Review header, and F2's shell part 'next' plus a palette action.

proposals.title: Every lost point gets a cause and a cure: Trap, Gap, Care, Time
proposals.what:
SERVER (F4): classify each wrong or blank answer when it is filed, into attempts.cause:
- TRAP: the picked option names a misconception (not the filler), or a typed grid-in value matches an spr_mistake.
- CARE: wrong on a type the student has right on at least 80% of their last 5 clean answers; or the filler 'near-miss arithmetic slip' was picked; or it was answered in under 40% of the type's target time (proposal 6).
- TIME: a blank in a timed sitting; a dwell under 15 s in the module's last 90 s (qstate ms and time left); or Time's up.
- GAP: everything else, e.g. a type never answered right, 2 or more first-try misses on it in 14 days, or 'I'm guessing'.

Each miss costs its slot value from the score engine (fallback: WEIGHT / possible x anchor slope), so a hard miss in upper module 2 costs more than an easy one in lower.

REPORT HERO (S6): a stacked bar 'Points lost ≈ 38 · Trap 14 · Gap 10 · Care 8 · Time 6'. Each segment has its cure:
- Trap: 'Repair 5 traps' (pool redo on those templates).
- Gap: 'Learn these 3 types' (worked example first, proposal 5).
- Care: 'Accuracy run' (10 easy or medium questions, untimed, aim 10 of 10).
- Time: 'Speed reps on your 3 slowest types' (proposal 6).

The same bar goes on the practice summary. Review Redo gets a Cause filter and a chip on each row. The Results overview adds 'Where your points went · last 30 days', by cause, with a trend.

CARE NUDGE (practice only, never in tests): when an easy question is answered faster than 40% of its target, a quiet 'Quick one. Re-read what it asks?' with a one-tap Check before submitting.

STUDENT DOES DIFFERENTLY: fixes the cause instead of 'doing more questions': re-reads easy ones, learns a type from an example, drills speed, or repairs a named trap. WHY IT MOVES THE SCORE: above about 600, careless and time losses are often the biggest and cheapest points, and more practice fixes neither.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep's report has Correct / Incorrect / Unanswered / Accuracy tiles and a per-domain %. The per-question payload has no skill, difficulty or time, and the gauge contradicts the tiles on blanks. Nothing says why a point was lost. The spec names the misconception on trap misses and has rushed-miss filters and a what-if line, but it gives no cause for each lost point and no cure for each cause.
proposals.needs: F4: attempts.cause column (§2.5), classification in progress.record and record_paper. S5 qstate: per-answer ms and time left (R7). Score engine for slot values. Proposal 6 targets (fallback 95 s). S6 report hero and Results card; S4 summary; S10 Redo filter; F5 presets 'accuracy_run' and 'speed'.

proposals.title: Spaced review of every question type you've learned: 'Due' for Math, never the same question twice
proposals.what:
SERVER (F4): a table type_state(learner, template, stage, box, due, last_clean, lapses), updated in progress.record.

STAGES: New → Learning (first answer) → Learned (2 clean first tries in a row) → Kept (passed a spaced review) → Proven (passed a review 30+ days out).

SCHEDULE: a clean first try on a due review moves the box up one; intervals are 3, 8, 21, 45 and 90 days. A miss drops to box 1 and opens a trap as now. EXAM CAP: every Learned type comes back at least once in the last 14 days before exam_date, and intervals shrink to fit the days left.

SERVING (F5): a new pool 'due' serves fresh seeds on due templates, never the exact question, at the tier last passed. It interleaves across skills (no two neighbours from one skill), so the student has to recognise the method. It replaces the static 'review' pool (right 10+ days ago) and the coach's keep_warm +30. R9's fixed-mistake check-ins use the same scheduler: a fixed trap's template enters at box 1. So there is one Due count.

SCREENS:
- Today list row: 'Due reviews · 12 types · about 14 min' (it ticks itself).
- Review nav meta: '12 due'.
- Review: a Due tab with a 14-day forecast bar chart, as in Words.
- Plan: a 'review' task sized to what is due, capped at 30% of the day.
- Builder 'Questions from': 'Due · 12'.
- Skill rows: 'Strong · fading' when at least half the skill's Learned types are overdue.
- Results, per skill: a type ladder, one cell per type (New / Learning / Learned / Kept / Proven), e.g. '23 types · 4 proven · 6 kept · 3 learning · 10 new'. 'Question types met 57 of 386' becomes '57 met · 31 kept'.
- Results retention line: 'Remembered after 3+ weeks: 84% (46 of 55 reviews)'.

STUDENT DOES DIFFERENTLY: opens each day with about 10 minutes of due types from several skills, each with new numbers. WHY IT MOVES THE SCORE: spaced retrieval is the most robust effect in learning research, and SAT Math is a few hundred recurring types; forgetting between August and test day is a silent leak. Interleaving the due types trains choosing the method, which blocked practice does not.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep spaces vocabulary only (and its Due Today stayed at 0 after grading); nothing in their Math ever comes back. A finite bank could not do it without re-showing questions whose keys the student has already seen. The spec re-checks only fixed mistakes, at 3/10/30 days, and has a 'right 10+ days ago' filter, so a type the student got right first time is never scheduled again.
proposals.needs: F4: type_state table (§2.5), update in progress.record, carry and LEARNER_TABLES. F5: pool 'due' (§2.6) with the exam cap and interleave. R9 folded into the same scheduler. S3 Today row; S7 review task; S10 Due tab and forecast; S6 type ladder and retention; F2 nav meta; the keep_warm pref becomes the on/off switch for due reviews.

proposals.title: Worked example first, hints that fade, and 'your way vs the right way'
proposals.what:
SEE A WORKED ONE (key W, practice only): on any question before answering, a panel opens beside it with a sibling seed of the same template. Seeds come from the 900000+ range, as /api/types/{t}/example uses, so it never gives the answer away. The panel shows:
- its stem and figure, with the key highlighted;
- the rationale as numbered steps, split at ', so', ';', '.' and 'then' (279 of 386 templates' rationales have 2 or more clauses, measured on one seed each);
- 'The traps': each wrong option's value with its misconception.
'Now yours' closes it. The answer is filed as assisted: half credit like a guess, and it never closes a trap (added to R8).

AUTOMATIC: after 2 first-try misses on one template within 14 days, the repair is preceded by a worked sibling ('Study this one first · about 30 s'). The repair after it can still close the trap.

HINTS (key T): Hint 1 is the first step of this question's own rationale, with its numbers. Hint 2 is 'Watch for: {the field's most common misconception on this type}' (S4 type stats; otherwise the template's first reason). Then Show answer. Using any hint files the answer as assisted.

NEW TYPES: when the coach or the due list serves a template the student has never answered, the strip offers 'New type · See a worked one'. It is not opened automatically.

CONTRAST ON A MISS: one line under the reveal, e.g. 'Your answer 432π/5 · used 360/θ in place of θ/360 | The key 15π/4 · 75/360 of 18π'.

BANK: T-bank adds an optional Item.steps (with this seed's numbers) to the 107 templates whose rationale is a single clause, family by family.

Never shown in tests, the challenge, contests, or the QOTD before answering.

STUDENT DOES DIFFERENTLY: on a type they cannot do, studies a solved twin and then solves their own, instead of guessing, missing and meeting the same trap again. WHY IT MOVES THE SCORE: for novices, worked examples beat repeated failed attempts (the worked-example effect), fading hints move them to solving alone, and honest half credit keeps mastery true.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep teaches nothing before or during a question. The QBank hides the key after a miss and lets you retry blind, and the QOTD does not even highlight the key. Their only teaching is one long explanation after the answer. Ours shows the same kind of problem solved with other numbers, which only a generator can make on demand. Its hints come from the question's own steps, and it never hands over this question's answer.
proposals.needs: F3: workspace 'example' panel, hint row and contrast line. F5: POST /api/drill/example {session, question_id} returning a sibling with rationale steps (R19 access; 900000+ seeds). F4: attempts.assisted added to R8 with guess semantics. S4 type stats (most common misconception). T-bank: Item.steps. Keyboard §2.8, runner scope: W worked example, T hint (both free today).

proposals.title: Pacing that is trained: per-type time targets, a time bank and speed reps
proposals.what:
TARGETS: each template's target is the median time of right first tries across all learners (n>=20); before that, the tier defaults are easy 60 s, medium 95 s, hard 130 s (a mean of about 95 s, R34). Served with the question as target_ms.

AFTER ANSWERING: '0:48 · target 0:55', and a 'Right but slow' tag above 1.5x the target.

TIME BANK: in any timed set, and as the tests' pace guide (prefs.test_pace), one figure in the top bar: '+1:40' ahead or '-0:55' behind, the sum of (target - used) over answered questions. In tests it replaces the uniform pace line. Check your work adds 'At this pace you finish with 2:10 to spare' or '3 questions short'.

SPEED REPS (F5, speed:true): a set of one skill's 'right but slow' types. Each question has its own countdown, 1.25x its target, tightening to 1.0x after 3 on time in a row. Over-time answers still count for mastery but not as 'on pace'. Summary: 'On pace 7 of 10 · median 0:58 → 0:47'.

TWO-PASS TRAINING: in timed practice modules, pref two_pass nudges once when a question passes 2x its target: 'Skip (S) and come back'. The summary and report show 'Second pass: 3 answered, 2 right'.

RESULTS PACE PANEL: median vs target for each skill, and 'Last 5 minutes of modules: 48% right vs 71% before' (from qstate ms and time left).

STUDENT DOES DIFFERENTLY: learns which types they must do faster, drills exactly those against a clock sized to the type, and practises skip-and-return. WHY IT MOVES THE SCORE: blanks and rushed guesses at the end of module 2 are lost points, and speed on routine types buys time for hard ones. A single 1:35 alert cannot tell a slow easy question from a normal hard one.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep has a per-question stopwatch that resets on reload, Timed | Untimed, and a contest-only 'average seconds by difficulty' chart. The spec has one 1:35 alert for every question and a 'your average on this type' line. Neither sets a target per type, keeps a running time bank, or drills speed.
proposals.needs: attempts ms/sms (R7, R8); S4 type stats for crowd medians (open question 12 threshold); F3 time bank in the runner top bar and Check your work; F5 drill fields speed, per-question limit and two_pass; S5 test pace guide; S6 report and Results pace panels; proposal 3's Time cause.

proposals.title: A mistake counts as fixed only when the fix transfers and lasts, in the student's own words
proposals.what:
CHECK-IN RULE (R9 change):
- The 10-day check-in is served from a different template that carries the same normalised misconception. 79 norms recur across 2 or more templates and 12 across topics (progress.related(norm) + the drill's want regex).
- If there is none, it is the same template one tier up when that exists, otherwise a fresh seed.
- The 30-day check-in is timed at the type's target (proposal 6).
- Passing both sets closed_how='transfer', shown in Review's Fixed tab as 'Fixed · held on a different question type'.
- A miss on the transfer check reopens the mistake as Relapsed, with 'It came back on {other type}'.

YOUR RULE: when a trap opens, the reveal offers an optional one-line field 'Next time I will…' (up to 120 characters; placeholder from the misconception, e.g. 'check θ/360, not 360/θ'). It is stored in traps.note (already in §2.5). It shows above the question on every repair and check-in of that trap, and can be edited there.

MY RULES: a Review page listing every rule by skill, printable as one sheet. The plan's Final phase puts 'Read your rules · 5 min' on the eve.

FIXED LOG: when true, a relapse insight such as '4 of 5 relapses happened in timed sittings'.

STUDENT DOES DIFFERENTLY: writes one sentence about each new mistake, and proves the fix days later on a different kind of question. WHY IT MOVES THE SCORE: two clean answers on one template can be pattern-matching; delayed retrieval on a new surface is what holds on test day, and explaining the error in their own words improves retention.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep's redo list is filled by an API no screen calls, so it is always empty, and nothing ever re-checks a mistake. The spec closes a mistake after 2 clean answers on the same template and re-checks it on that same template.
proposals.needs: F4: R9 serving rule, closed_how 'transfer', progress.related. F5: want regex on the checks pool. F3: rule line on the workspace. S10: Fixed-tab labels and the My rules page with print CSS. S7: eve task. traps.note already exists.

proposals.title: A skill map that says how sure it is, and practice that fills the gaps
proposals.what:
BADGES: every skill row (UI.skillRow on Me, Results, the builder and Plan) shows mastery with a measurement badge from the score engine's posterior:
- Measured: interval ±0.1 or tighter
- Rough
- Not measured
A whisker on the bar draws the interval.

EXPLORATION: while any skill is Rough or Not measured, coach sets and plan focus sets give it 1 slot in 10, tagged 'Checking Probability' in the question's why. This stops once every skill has 8 clean answers across at least 2 tiers.

QUICK PLACEMENT (new drill kind 'placement', about 15 questions, about 20 min, untimed):
- Each question goes to the (skill, tier) with the widest interval, weighted by blueprint share.
- Up a tier after a right answer, down after a miss.
- It stops when every domain's interval is within ±0.15, or at 18 questions.
- Result: the skill map, a first practice estimate, and suggested plan focus.
- Offered on Plan step 1 ('Measure me · 15 questions', beside the sliders), on Today for a new student ('Find where you stand · 15 questions'), and whenever more than 6 skills are Not measured.
- Fresh seeds every time, no sign-up gate (unlike the diagnostic), and it counts as normal practice.

PLAN STEP 4: Focus is pre-set from the score engine's points (top 2 domains, up to 6 skills), each row reading e.g. '+18 points available · 54% on medium'. The student can change any of it.

STUDENT DOES DIFFERENTLY: measures in 20 minutes instead of guessing their level, and cannot silently skip a skill. WHY IT MOVES THE SCORE: time on skills already known is wasted, a plan built on a guess works on the wrong domains, and a badge stops a student reading 2 lucky answers as Strong.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep's plan starts from sliders the student sets (it uses results only when both sections are above 200) and from Focus/Normal/Strong picked by hand for 8 domains. Their domain % rests on 1-8 questions. The spec prefills from tests and suggests the weakest worked domain, but its mastery bar shows no uncertainty, so 3 answers look as certain as 300.
proposals.needs: Score engine posteriors (F4 estimate.py); F5 drill 'placement' plus exploration slots in drill._pick with the why tag; F1 UI.skillRow badge and whisker; S7 step 1 and step 4 prefill; S3 new-student Up next; S1 and S6 skill rows.

proposals.title: Desmos, loaded with this exact question
proposals.what:
BANK (T-bank): graphable templates get desmos(params) -> list[str], this seed's expressions, plus a one-line move ('Tap the intersection · x = 3'). Candidates: systems_of_linear_equations 20, nonlinear_equations_and_systems 32, linear and nonlinear functions 59, linear_inequalities 18, equivalent_expressions 21. Start with the two systems topics and grow family by family, like spr_mistakes.

AFTER ANSWERING (practice, the review pane and the report player): 'Solve it in Desmos' loads the expressions into the docked calculator (UI.calc → setExpression). The move appears under the rationale as a second solution, with 'By hand · median 1:40 | With Desmos · about 0:30'. Never offered before answering, in a live test, the challenge or a contest (R19).

CALCULATOR SKILLS (builder preset): graphable types with the calculator docked open and the time bank on. The summary compares the student's times with and without it.

BUILDER: a 'Desmos-friendly' chip on TypeRow, and a filter.

STUDENT DOES DIFFERENTLY: learns to solve linear, quadratic and system questions with the graphing calculator the real test provides. WHY IT MOVES THE SCORE: those skills are most of the 70% of the section in Algebra and Advanced Math. Graphing is faster and avoids algebra slips, which is why tutors teach it first.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep embeds the same Desmos panel in the QBank and the exam, and never shows how to use it on a question. Ours opens the calculator with this question's equations already typed, because the template knows its own numbers.
proposals.needs: T-bank: per-template desmos expressions. F3: UI.calc setExpression API with dock. R19: access only after answering. Open question 15: a production Desmos key. F5: preset and filter. S4: builder chip.

proposals.title: Confidence on every answer, and blind spots fixed first
proposals.what:
CONFIDENCE ROW: practice's single 'I'm guessing' becomes a 3-way row under the options: Sure · Unsure · Guess. K cycles it in practice and in tests, where test_confidence stays. New pref 'confidence', on by default in practice. One tap, optional; untouched means no data. Stored per answer in attempts.conf; record_paper copies qstate.conf. Guess is R8's guess (half credit). Unsure + right opens an Unsure item, as R9 does now.

BLIND SPOTS: misconceptions picked while marked Sure. Each gets a 'Blind spot' chip in Review Redo, sorts first there, and is the coach's first priority. It needs 3 clean answers to close instead of 2. The reveal on a Sure miss reads 'You were sure. This is a belief to fix, not a slip.'

RESULTS CALIBRATION CARD: 3 bars, e.g. 'Sure 91% right · Unsure 58% · Guess 31%', over the last 30 days with a trend, plus a test-day tip computed from it: 'Your Unsure answers are right 58%. On test day, answer, flag, move on.'

STUDENT DOES DIFFERENTLY: taps how sure they are, and fixes confident errors first. WHY IT MOVES THE SCORE: high-confidence errors are the misconceptions that repeat on test day, and they are corrected best when flagged as surprising (hypercorrection). Calibration tells a student when to trust a first answer and when to flag it.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep has no confidence signal anywhere. The spec has Sure/Unsure/Guess in tests (off by default) and a guessing toggle in practice, and shows calibration only inside one test report.
proposals.needs: F3: workspace confidence row. F4: attempts.conf (§2.5), R8/R9 rules for Sure misses (3 owed). New prefs key 'confidence' (§2.7); keyboard §2.8 (K in practice). S10: Blind spot chip and sort. S6: calibration card.

proposals.title: Proof of progress, at the moment it happens
proposals.what:
- VERDICT LINE: when a clean first try lands on a template the student missed at least twice before, it adds 'Missed 3 times in September · now 4 in a row' (from attempts).
- MISTAKE CLOSED: 'Fixed · Arc length: θ/360 · took 6 days, 5 questions'.
- YOUR WEEK: a card on Today every Monday, and on the Results overview. It shows points gained (the practice estimate's change), mistakes fixed, check-ins passed, types moved to Kept or Proven, minutes against the goal and the best day. It has 'Send to a parent or tutor' through the progress link (R18a).
- THEN AND NOW: a Results toggle that shows the skill map on the plan's start day (mastery can be recomputed from attempts for any date) next to today's.
- ACHIEVEMENTS: tiers tied to these facts: types Proven 10 / 50 / 150, points gained 20 / 50 / 100.

STUDENT DOES DIFFERENTLY: sees evidence of improvement every day, not only after a test. WHY IT MOVES THE SCORE: feeling competence grow keeps practice going better than streak pressure alone, and weekly points and fixed mistakes make slow progress visible between tests.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep's achievements are four hard-coded tiles with a dead View All, their two streaks disagree, and nothing ever says 'you got better at X'. The spec has a this-week-vs-last row and achievements, but nothing marks the moment an old weakness becomes a strength.
proposals.needs: F4: queries over attempts and traps. Score engine delta; proposal 4 stages. S4: verdict line. S3: weekly card. S6: then-and-now toggle. S1: achievement rules (R25). R18a: progress link.

proposals.title: Reminders that say what is due, at the time the student chose
proposals.what:
SETTINGS → Study: 'Remind me at 19:00' (prefs.study_time), with the channel Push (installed app, where supported) or Email (when an email is saved and SMTP is set).

The reminder carries today's content from /api/next, e.g. '4 check-ins and 8 due types · about 12 min · 3-day streak'.

EVENING NUDGE: at most one, at 21:00 local, and only when the day's minimum is not met and the streak is at risk. None on plan rest days, none once the goal is met, nothing between 22:00 and 07:00. One-tap unsubscribe.

WEEKLY DIGEST (opt-in email): the Your week card (proposal 11), sent to the student and, if they choose, to the holder of their progress link.

SERVICE WORKER: used for push only; nothing is cached.

STUDENT DOES DIFFERENTLY: at the time they picked, gets a nudge naming a concrete 12-minute task. WHY IT MOVES THE SCORE: the most common way daily practice stops is not starting, and a specific small task at a fixed time (an implementation intention) raises follow-through.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep asks for 'Preferred time: Evening' and does nothing with it. The spec puts a static .ics alarm in the calendar ('without a notification system'), which cannot say what is due or stay quiet on a rest day.
proposals.needs: A push-only service worker (this reverses Shell §2.14's 'no service worker'). VAPID keys and a Web Push sender (a pywebpush dependency; or ship email only first through mail.py). A push_subs table (F4 §2.5); prefs.remind gains a channel. Content from proposal 2. SMTP (open question 5). On iOS, push needs the installed app.

proposals.title: Play today: the whole day in one run, started with one tap
proposals.what:
Entry points: Today's Up next pill becomes `Start today · 4 parts · 38 min` (autofocused, so Enter starts it). The sidebar Today card and the phone Today tab show `Continue today · part 2 of 4`. It is also the first Suggested row in the palette.

New `GET /api/today/run` (S3) returns ordered parts `{kind, title, count, minutes, why, pts, status, sid?}`:
1. `due`: mistakes due a check-in (pool `checks`) plus keep-warm types (pool `review`), at most 6 questions.
2. `fix`: the top open mistakes by points (pool `redo`, level `as_missed`).
3. `focus`: the plan's or the coach's set.
4. `daily`: the two day's questions, if they are unanswered.
5. `words`: due cards when `words_goal > 0`. This part hands off to `/words/run/?id=&then=run` and comes back.
6. `test`: on a plan test day only, last, handed off to the lobby.

The challenge is offered after the summary, never inside the run, because of its ranked rules. The budget is the plan day's minutes, else the daily goal, else 20 min. Focus shrinks first; due and fix never drop below 2 questions.

Each drill part is an ordinary drill session with `cfg.run = 'YYYY-MM-DD'` and `cfg.part = kind`. History, plan auto-completion, study time and Results therefore work unchanged, and no table is added.

Runner:
- One ProgressRail split into labelled parts (`Check-ins 2/3 · Fix 0/6 · Circles + 1 · Day's 2`).
- The runner swaps session ids between drill parts, so there is no page load.
- Between parts, an in-runner card: `Fix done · 5 of 6 · 2 mistakes fixed · Next: Circles + Percentages · 14 q`, with Continue (Enter), `Skip this part` (S) and `Stop for today` (Esc; keeps your place).

The end is one Day summary: minutes against the goal ring, questions, right %, mistakes fixed and opened, check-ins held, points moved (proposal 3) and the streak day. Its actions are `Today's challenge · 10 q` and `Keep going · 10 more`.

`/practice/session/?run=today` resumes the first unfinished part on any device. On a phone the interstitial is a full card with a 56px Continue pill in thumb reach.

States:
- Nothing due: that part is left out.
- Rest day: `Practice anyway · 3 parts`.
- All done: `Day done · 42 of 40 min` and `Keep going`.
proposals.beats: Their Today's Plan card launches one task at a time (Dashboard → Full Plan → Start task). QBank sessions never end, so nothing comes back, and every task needs a manual 'Mark done'. A 4-task day costs about 12 clicks, 4 page loads and 4 ticks, and the dashboard still doesn't know what you did. Ours is 1 tap plus Enter between parts, completes itself, and ends in one summary. Their only spaced 'Due Today' is for vocab. Ours puts mistake check-ins (3/10/30 days), keep-warm types and due words into one Due part.
proposals.needs: S3 `/api/today/run` and the Up next state. S7 `plan.today_summary()` supplies parts and minutes. F5 drill body: pools checks/review/redo, `cfg.run`/`cfg.part`, `source:'run'`. F3 runner: multi-part rail, interstitial, session swap. S4 session page `?run=`. S9 words run `then=` return. S8 offers the challenge at the end. F2 shows `Continue today` in the sidebar metas and the palette. Proposal 3 supplies the per-part points.

proposals.title: Worked steps with this question's own numbers, checked against the key, plus a hint ladder
proposals.what:
Grounding: I generated one item per template (382 templates, seed 777). 94% of rationales are a single sentence, median 91 characters, for example 'Every term holds at least one w and a factor of 10, so 10w comes out and each exponent drops by one.' Our per-option misconceptions beat their Distractor Analysis, but our Justification is thinner than their long-form one.

Bank (T-bank): a new field `Item.steps: list[str]`, 2 to 5 lines built by each template from its own `item.params` with this seed's numbers. Example: `1. The diameter is 14, so the radius is 14 ÷ 2 = 7.` `2. Area = πr² = π · 7² = 49π.` An optional `Item.step_of_reason: {reason: step index}` says where each named misconception goes wrong.

An audit check requires the last step's value to equal the key (`numeral` or `norm_text` match). A worked solution can therefore never disagree with the key or with the independent solver. `tools/steps_coverage.py` prints `n of 386 templates show steps`. It ships at partial coverage, with templates ordered by attempt count.

Verdict (F3 workspace, in every mode that reveals):
- `Steps ▾` sits under the rationale. It is open on a miss and collapsed on a right answer; `prefs.rationale` governs.
- Steps are numbered lines in Source Serif at `--q-opt`, with numbers in DM Mono.
- On a named miss, the diverging step carries a line `You went wrong here: used the diameter as the radius`.

Hint ladder (practice only; never in exams, contests or the day's questions):
- A `Hint` tool in the question strip, key `W`, labelled `Hint 1 of 3`. Each press reveals the next step except the last.
- A hinted answer files as `guess=1`: half credit, never closes a mistake (R8). The verdict says `With 1 hint`, and `qstate[qid].hints` stores the count.
- Templates without steps show the rationale exactly as today. Nothing says 'missing'.
proposals.beats: Their explanation is one long AI-prose 'Justification: … Distractor Analysis:', shown only after answering, never pointing at your own error, and unverified. Ours is numbered and uses your numbers. It marks the exact step your named mistake broke, is proven against the key by the same audit that ships the item, and can be opened one step at a time before answering, which they cannot do at all.
proposals.needs: T-bank: templates emit steps and step_of_reason, plus the audit check and the coverage script. F5/S4: `practice.to_question` carries steps, hidden until reveal like the key. F3: render, the Hint tool and key W. F4: the guess flag on hinted answers and `hints` in qstate. S6 and S10 render steps in the review player and pane.

proposals.title: Points on the table: one score-value unit on every mistake, skill and task
proposals.what:
F4 adds `estimate.points(learner)`, which returns `{total, by_topic:[{topic, pts, acc_now, acc_goal, share, basis_n}], by_trap:{id: pts}}`:
- `share` is the topic's expected share of a Math section's weighted points: the BLUEPRINT domain share × the topic's share within its domain from `blueprint.kinds()`, weighted by `scoring.WEIGHT` over the tier mix.
- `acc_goal = max(0.85, the accuracy the target band needs)`.
- `pts = slope of scoring.ANCHORS at the learner's weighted fraction × share × (acc_goal − acc_now)`, rounded to 5. It is hidden below 10 first tries ('not measured yet').
- A trap's pts = its topic's pts × (the trap's hits ÷ the topic's misses in the last 60 days).
- `total = Σ` over topics, capped at 800 minus the estimate midpoint.
- Cached per learner and refreshed on answer write.

One chip style: DM Mono 12px `≈ +10 pts` in `--soft`, never orange. Tapping it opens proposal 7's popover with the arithmetic in words: 'Circles is about 5% of a section's weighted points. You're at 48% first-try, the goal is 85%. At your level (between 480 and 620) that's about 560 scaled points per whole section, so ≈ +10.'

Where it shows:
- Today: hero chip `≈ 80 points on the table`, the Up next reason (`3 open mistakes · worth ≈ +20`) and the Review card rows.
- Review Redo: new sort `Points` (the default) and a `Most points` preset.
- Results skills table: column `On the table`, default sort descending, with domain totals.
- Plan's `Why this?`, the palette's skill rows and the report's what-if line (same function).
- Play today's summary: `≈ +10 moved today`.
proposals.beats: Theirs offers one sentence, 'Weakest first. This is where your remaining time pays off most.' (Plan Progress tab only), and one overall 'Score gap (1000 now, 1400 target)'. Their domain copy is mislabelled ('13% of test section, 1-8 questions'). Nothing of theirs says which mistake or skill is worth fixing first. Ours ranks every mistake, skill and task in the unit students think in, with the same number on every page and the arithmetic one tap away.
proposals.needs: F4 `estimate.py` using `scoring.ANCHORS`/`WEIGHT` and `progress.BLUEPRINT`. F5 `blueprint.kinds()` for per-topic shares. Consumers: S3, S6, S7, S10, F2 (palette), S4 (summary). Proposal 7's popover. The heuristics join open question 12.

proposals.title: Learn any of 386 types in a minute: worked example, then three of your own
proposals.what:
Entry points:
- `Learn this type` on palette type rows (Shift+Enter), the Log-a-mistake type rows, the Results skill panel's type list, Review's family strip and the builder's type list.
- A quiet `First time? See a worked example` above a practice stem when `seen == 0` for that template.

Flow, in the inline runner (a 720px sheet on desktop, full screen on a phone):
1. `Example`: `GET /api/types/{t}/example` (seed 900000+), fully revealed. The key row, every wrong option with its named misconception, and the rationale and steps (proposal 2) are all open. `Your turn` (Enter).
2. `Your turn 1 of 3`: same template, fresh seed, instant feedback. A miss queues the repair as usual.
3. Two more at the same tier, or one tier up after two rights when the template spans tiers.
4. Card: `Circles · Central angle from an arc · 3 of 3 right · counted in your mastery`, with `Practise Circles · 10` and `Done`.

Server: `POST /api/drill {templates:[t], count:3, source:'learn'}`. The example is never an attempt. The 3 answers file normally and list in history as `Learn · Central angle from an arc`. Esc keeps it as an unfinished Learn set. Keys: A–D, Enter, Esc.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep never teaches. Every surface is a test, the explanation appears only after a miss, and a fixed bank has no second example of the same kind to try right after. Ours teaches any type in about a minute: an example with every trap labelled, then three fresh ones. It is 1 tap from wherever the student found the type.
proposals.needs: F5: `/api/types/{t}/example` and `source 'learn'`. F3: the inline runner mode. F2: the palette row action. S4 (builder, first-meet link), S6 (skill panel), S10 (family strip) and the quick sheet add the entry buttons. It works on today's rationales and gets better with proposal 2.

proposals.title: Instant by default: speed budgets, and the mechanisms that meet them
proposals.what:
Budgets go into §2.1 and I1's walk, measured by a Playwright script `tools/perf.py` on a seeded learner. It fails when a budget is missed on two consecutive runs:
- Check → verdict painted ≤ 100 ms p95 locally.
- Next → next question painted ≤ 50 ms, with no network call.
- Any revisited page: cached content ≤ 150 ms, fresh data ≤ 600 ms.
- Today first-visit LCP ≤ 1.5 s on Slow 4G on a mid phone.
- CLS 0 from data arriving.

Mechanisms:
(a) `POST /api/drill/{id}/answer` also returns `next`, the following question already chosen with the repair logic. Today every question costs two round trips (answer, then `/next`; verified in `server/app.py`). The runner pre-renders the next stem, KaTeX and figures into a hidden node while the student reads the verdict. `/next` stays for skip and jumps.
(b) `UI.api` serves GETs stale-while-revalidate: each response is kept in sessionStorage per path and learner (try/catch, 2 MB LRU). Pages paint cached data at once and patch numbers in place. Skeletons appear only on a true first view.
(c) `head.js` adds Speculation Rules: `prerender` the Up next target and `prefetch` the five tab destinations at `eagerness: moderate`. Never on `/test/` or session URLs, and pages must not POST on load.
(d) Cross-document View Transitions: `@view-transition {navigation: auto}` with a 120 ms fade of `main` only. The sidebar and tabs are pinned with `view-transition-name`. Off under reduced motion or `prefs.motion=reduce`.
(e) Optimistic toggles (save, mark, skip, prefs, plan skip/move) flip at once and revert with a toast on failure.
(f) The runner never waits on non-critical calls (crowd line, family strip, history); they fill in afterwards.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep is a client-routed SPA, so their route changes are fast after the first load. Ours is 14+ static pages, each reloading and re-fetching behind skeletons, and would feel slower than theirs without this. Their cards skeleton-load on each visit (the comments modal 'opens with skeleton then loads') and their plan builder plays a fake progress screen. With this, our questions change with zero wait, every revisited page opens painted, and the speed is measured, not hoped for.
proposals.needs: F2: ui.js API cache and head.js speculation rules. F1: view-transition CSS. F3: the runner consumes `next` and pre-renders. F5/S4: the answer response carries `next`. I1: `tools/perf.py` and the budget gate.

proposals.title: Re-check now: an instant, independent verdict when a student says the key is wrong
proposals.what:
In `UI.report`, choosing `Answer key is wrong` (only once the verdict has been shown) immediately calls `POST /api/report/check {session, question_id, answer}`. The server regenerates (template, seed) and runs `satbank.audit.audit(item)`, whose solver re-derives the answer from `item.params` alone. I timed it: one item per template, 385 audited, 161 ms total, about 0.4 ms each. It returns `{holds, derived:'49π', your:{value:'196π', mistake:'used the diameter as the radius'}|null, steps?}`.

When the key holds, the form shows before Send:
- `Re-checked just now by an independent solver: the answer is 49π.`
- When the student's answer matches a named reason or spr_mistake: `Your 196π is what you get if you used the diameter as the radius.`
- `Show steps` (proposal 2).
- Buttons: `That explains it` (closes without a report and logs a `check_only` count) and `Still send the report` (the form continues).

When the audit fails (a real bank bug):
- The form shows `You're right: our check disagrees with this key. It won't count against you.`
- The attempt is set `disputed=1` without using one of the 5 dispute slots.
- The report is created with `status:'confirmed'`.
- The template joins a quarantine list (kv `quarantine`), which drill, test, contest and QOTD selection skip until a fix ships. The admin page lists quarantined templates first.

Never offered while a sitting is live, since marking never shows then.
proposals.beats: Their report goes into silence: the student never learns what happened, and the key stays until staff look. Ours answers in under a second from an independent solver and names the student's own misconception when that is the real cause. A truly broken template is pulled from every student's feed automatically. Only a bank where every item is re-derived by a second solver can do this.
proposals.needs: F6: `reports.py` endpoint and the modal step. The existing `satbank.audit`. F4: the disputed-flag path. F5 (drill), S5 (tests), S8 (contests) and S3 (QOTD) skip quarantined templates in selection. F6 admin page ordering.

proposals.title: One study vocabulary: the same few verbs, keys and icons in every section
proposals.what:
The spec names our core power (new numbers on demand) in many ways. Counted in rebuild-v2.md: 'Another like this' 6, 'Another one like this' 4, 'Try one like this' 7, 'Fresh one like this' 6, 'New one like this' 4, '5 more like this' 3, 'Fresh versions' 11, 'Again · new questions' 3, 'Practice again' 5, 'Try one now' 6, 'Drill it' 4. The exact-replay and fix actions add 'Again, exactly', 'Start over with these exact questions', 'Fix N', 'Fix these', 'Redo these', 'Twin test' and 'Retake as a test'.

Kit `UI.VERBS` (F1) defines four verbs. Each has one label, one icon and one helper line (tooltip and `?` sheet); the keys are those §2.8 already gives:
- `One like this` / `N like these` (T in players and lists, and in the runner after a verdict): same type, new numbers. Helper: `New numbers · counts toward mastery`.
- `Again, exactly` (E in players and lists; not offered inside a running set, where E is eliminate): same question. Helper: `Same question · doesn't count toward mastery`.
- `Fix` (a set on the misses; new numbers). Helper: `Two clean answers close each mistake`.
- `Test like this` (a parallel form of a sitting). Helper: `Same question types, new numbers, scored like any test`.

Every section's copy uses only these. I1 adds a grep over `web/` for the retired phrases, which must return nothing.
proposals.beats: Their actions are few and generic ('More practice', 'Practice again'), and their fixed bank can't offer most of ours. Ours are more capable, but about 18 names for 4 ideas would make them hard to learn. One vocabulary with fixed keys turns our advantage into a habit: T for 'another like this', everywhere.

proposals.title: Thumb-first runner on phones
proposals.what:
At 390px (F3 runner/workspace):
- The question strip keeps only number · skill · difficulty.
- The row of 7 tiny captioned tools (Mark · Eliminate · Highlight · Note · Details · Report · Attempts), today at the top, moves into a 48px tool tray directly above RunFooter: Mark, Eliminate, Calculator, Hint (proposal 2), and `⋯` for the rest in a sheet.

Gestures:
- Long-press an option (450 ms) to strike or unstrike, with an Undo toast.
- Swipe horizontally on the question body for Next / Previous, only where moving is free (end mode, review, after a verdict), never before Check in instant mode.
- Swipe up on the NavPill to open the navigator sheet.

proposals.title: Trap-true twins, and one Twin control on every question
proposals.what:
The problem, measured on the bank: a fresh seed of the same template leaves out the misconception the student picked 40.8% of the time. That is 10,802 of 26,469 trap and seed pairs, over 12 seeds per template, in 273 of the 386 templates. It is still 39.6% when letters and units are folded together, because each item draws only 3 of its template's mistakes. So the spec's repair ('the same template on a fresh seed', §3.3.4) and its rule that 'two clean answers on the template close the mistake' often never offer the trap again.

The fix:
(1) drill._fresh takes `trap: norm`. It walks seeds from a start derived from (learner, template, n), skips seeds already in attempts(learner, template, seed), and takes the first item whose reasons, or spr_mistakes, normalise to that norm. Measured: 98.4% of traps come back within 60 seeds, with a median walk of 1 seed and a 90th percentile of 7, at 0.26 ms a seed. If nothing is found, it serves the plain twin with the line 'This type didn't offer that trap again; here is the closest.'
(2) progress.record stores the norms each attempt offered. A trap's owed count drops only on clean answers to items that offered its norm. Other clean answers still count for mastery.
(3) Every repair, redo, check-in (R9), Spot the trap, Try one like this and QOTD 'like' drill passes `trap` whenever a trap exists.
(4) One verb, 'Twin', replaces 'Another one like this', 'Try one like this', 'Fresh one like this', '5 more like this', 'Another like this' and 'New one like this'. It has one glyph (two offset squares) and key T, which is free in §2.8's runner map. T works after answering in the runner and anywhere in the player.
(5) `UI.twin(anchor, ctx)` opens a menu:
   - Twin: the same trap if you missed, else the same type.
   - Easier / Harder: the same template when it has that tier (59 do), else the same skill at that tier, and labelled so.
   - Same trap in other types (n): a want-regex walk across templates that share the norm; 79 norms recur.
   - Twin x5: an inline set.
   - Print 10: a worksheet with a key.
(6) A twin's header reads 'Twin · watch for: used the diameter as the radius'. The pref twin_tell (default on) controls it; turning it off gives honest self-testing.
(7) Sittings, sets, worksheets and contests say 'Twin test' / 'Twin this set' with the same glyph.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep's QOTD 'More practice' and QBank retries either re-show the same item, with unlimited retries, or open a generic list. A fixed bank cannot make a new question that contains the exact trap you fell for. This also makes our own core promise true: today it holds only about 59% of the time.
proposals.needs: F5: extend _fresh's want walk from 12 to 60 seeds, match spr_mistakes too, and add the `trap` field to the §2.6 drill body. F4: store offered norms on attempts and change the closing rule in R9 and progress.record. F3: UI.twin and the T key in the runner and player maps. Every question surface swaps its own button for UI.twin: S3 QOTD and Try one now, S4 verdict, S6 player, S8 contest review, S9 word examples, S10 pane.

proposals.title: Points on the table: one score-gain forecast that ranks everything
proposals.what:
A new `server/points.py`.

Model:
(1) For each skill and each type the learner has met, p is the chance of a clean first-try right answer, by tier. It comes from the learner's clean attempts (R8 rules: no repeat, disputed or void rows; a guess counts half), shrunk toward the field's first-try rate on that template and tier (k = 8). Once Compete fills item_ratings and learner ratings, p = logistic(rating minus item rating).
(2) The expected Math section walks blueprint.slots() for module 1 and for both module 2s. It sums WEIGHT x p per slot (a domain's skills in proportion to blueprint.by_domain), routes with ROUTE_UP_AT, caps with LOWER_ROUTE_CEILING and scales with scoring._interpolate. These are the same functions that mark a real sitting.
(3) A skill's gain is the expected score with that skill's p raised to 0.85 (STRONG), minus the score now. The low and high ends come from evidence n.
(4) Minutes to that gain = questions to reach Strong (from the learner's own rate of mastery per answer, 12 per +0.1 by default) x the learner's median seconds on that skill.
(5) A route line appears when expected module-1 right answers are within 1.5 questions of 14/22: 'About 1 question short of the harder module 2. The lower route caps you at 580.'

Why it matters: under the blueprint, one Advanced Math skill carries about 11.7% of the section's points and one PSDA skill about 2.1%. That is a 5x difference no student knows by feel.

API: `GET /api/points` returns {now:{low,high}, route:{short_by, gain}, skills:[{topic, gain:[lo,hi], minutes, per_hour, why}], traps:[{id, gain}], types:[top 20]}. It is cached per learner until the next answer.

Where it shows (one hook per owner):
* Today, Up next: the reason line gains '≈ +12 points · 18 min', and progress.coach adds a points-per-minute term to its score.
* Results: a 'Points on the table' card with 19 range bars sorted by gain, minutes and a Practise button on each row, a sort of Points | Per hour, and a total ('about +60 available from 560–700').
* Plan: step 4's 'Use suggestions' picks the top skills by points per hour. The SplitBar labels what each share buys, and the plan's trajectory is now + the gains bought by the planned minutes.
* Review: Redo sorts by 'Most points' by default, with '≈ +3' on each row.
* Report: the what-if line uses this model.
* Palette, Suggested: 'Biggest win: Nonlinear functions · +18'.

Copy always says 'about' and shows a range, and links to a Help anchor, 'How points are estimated', which carries scoring.py's own statement that the scale is a heuristic.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep's plan Progress tab offers 'Accuracy by domain, weakest first' and an aiReason, and its dashboard shows no score until a full four-module test. Nothing there turns a weakness into points and minutes, weighs a skill by its share of the test, or knows about the routing cliff. Pricing each skill needs clean evidence per type, which only fresh, never-repeated items give.
proposals.needs: F4: clean-attempt rules and estimate.py. The blueprint module's slots and by_domain functions (blueprint.py, owned by S5). scoring._interpolate. Field first-try rates per template and tier (S4's per-type stats). item_ratings (S8), optional. Consumers: S3, S6, S7, S10, S1 (Me), F2 (palette). Add a §2.9 contract line: F4 or a new owner provides points.forecast(learner).

proposals.title: Autopilot: 'Study 30 min', one interleaved session that runs the whole day
proposals.what:
Where it launches:

* The same launcher in the sidebar Today card, the Q sheet and the palette ('study 20'), plus a manifest shortcut.

How it picks: `POST /api/drill {pool:'auto', minutes:N}` makes one practice sitting whose next_question picks each item when it is asked, in this order:
(1) Check-ins due (pool checks).
(2) Open traps ranked by points, as trap-true twins.
(3) The plan's focus topics, else the points engine's top skills, at the adaptive tier (R33).
(4) One keep-warm item (pool review) every 8th question.

Interleaving rules:
* Never the same template twice in a row.
* At most 3 of one skill in a row.
* The repair after a miss comes 1 to 3 questions later, not at once, so it is spaced.

In the runner: the top bar shows a goal ring ('18 of 30 min') and a chip naming the segment and why ('Check-in · fixed Sep 12', 'Fixing · sign of the slope', 'Focus · Circles'). There is no per-question countdown.

End: at N minutes the set ends at the next question boundary with a summary. It shows minutes, answered, mistakes closed, check-ins passed, the skills that moved (before → after bars) and '≈ +4 points banked' (the points delta), with 'Keep going · 10 min' and 'Done'.

Plan and history: every answer is tagged with the plan task it serves (fix, recheck or focus, by topic), so Today's list ticks itself and the day is done by the minutes rule. Pause and Save & exit work as in any set. History lists it as 'Autopilot · 30 min'.

proposals.title: Habit profile: the few mistakes behind all your mistakes
proposals.what:
The habit list: a fixed list of 14 habit classes, each normalised misconception tagged with one:
* answered the wrong quantity (the other solution, an intermediate value, a given value)
* sign slip
* operation swap
* part vs whole
* inverted ratio / wrong base
* squares and roots
* distribution / order of operations
* formula mix (radius/diameter, area/perimeter, sine/tangent)
* units and conversion
* misread graph or table
* slope vs intercept
* statistics mix-up
* probability denominator
* arithmetic slip

Tagging: `satbank/habits.py` holds an ordered regex list plus per-template overrides. A first regex pass already tags 52% of the 2,125 distinct normalised reasons; the goal is 95% with overrides, the rest 'other'. A coverage script prints the share. Each habit also gets one authored 'tell', 14 lines written once (e.g. 'Before solving, underline what the last sentence asks for').

Screens:
* A Habits card on Results and Me, ranked: 'Answered the wrong quantity · 31% of your misses · 9 types in 5 skills', with a 12-week sparkline and the field's rate.
* Per habit:
   - Habit drill · 10: a want-regex drill across every template whose reasons carry that habit, mixed skills, trap-true.
   - Spot it · 8: Spot the trap on that habit.
   - Trap maker: 'Type what a student who adds instead of multiplies would get', a grid-in checked against the Mis value.
* The report groups a sitting's misses by habit.
* Review filters by habit.

Cue (pref habit_cues, on): in practice, on a type that carries your top habit, a one-line tell shows above the options before any selection, so it can never depend on your choice or leak the key. It fades after 3 clean answers on that type, and is never shown in tests or contests.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep's 'Distractor Analysis' is prose per item. Its distractors carry no labels, so it can never see that half of a student's misses in five different skills are one habit. Only a bank with a named misconception behind every wrong option can add them up across topics and then drill that habit on fresh questions.
proposals.needs: T-bank or F4: a habit tag on each norm (relates to open question 18, Mis.tag). F5: want across templates. S6: Results card and report grouping. S1: Me. S4: the cue in the session. S10: Spot and the habit filter.

proposals.title: First visit: 'Find your next 50 points' in 12 questions, no account, no gate
proposals.what:
New learner: for a learner with no attempts, Today's hero becomes one card: 'Find where your points are · 12 questions · about 12 min · no sign-up'.

The placement:
* 12 fresh questions weighted by the blueprint: Algebra 4, Advanced Math 4, PSDA 2, Geometry & Trig 2.
* The tier steps up or down per R33, untimed, with a visible pace chip.
* It is a normal drill (source 'start'), so it files mastery and mistakes.

The result, shown straight away:
* A wide, honest band: 'about 480–640 from 12 questions, a module tightens it'.
* The top 3 skills by points on the table, with minutes each.
* The named traps it caught.
* Actions: 'Start with Nonlinear functions · 10' (primary), 'Build my plan' (prefilled from this), 'Take a module for a tighter band'.
* 'Save to your email' comes after, as a banner, never before.

The diagnostic stays for a fuller reading.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep puts a Google sign-in wall in front of everything, and shows no score until a full four-module test. A student switching over gets a band, their three biggest point leaks and a first set in about 12 minutes, without making an account.
proposals.needs: F5: source 'start' with the adaptive rule. Points engine. S3: new-student state. S7: plan prefill from the result. A decision on R38 / open question 8 (the diagnostic's own gate).

proposals.title: Your SAT playbook and a real final week
proposals.what:
`/playbook/` is built live from the student's data and prints on one A4 or Letter page. It has six parts:
(1) Your 8 costliest traps, ranked by points. Each has its habit tell and one worked twin: key, the wrong option and why.
(2) Pace plan: your median per domain against 95 s. 'First pass: flag and skip these types; they take you 2:40+ and you get under 50%' lists the slowest, lowest-yield types, weighted by the blueprint. 'Bank these: fast and right'.
(3) Desmos list: verified-route types where your hand time is over 60 s.
(4) Grid-in rules you have broken: 5/6-character entries, fraction forms, taken from S5's validator rejections and wrong SPR entries.
(5) The math words you looked up.
(6) The test-day checklist.

Final-week mode starts when exam_date is 7 days away or less. Today leads with 'Final week':
* every fixed mistake is brought forward as a check-in sweep, spread over the days;
* one full section at the real test's start time on a matching day (the doors-close time from the countdown);
* no new types;
* the playbook on the eve, which stays a rest day.

The plan's Final phase uses the same rules.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep's last week looks like any other week, with a countdown. A one-page personal trap sheet with a worked twin per trap, a skip list from your own timings and a Desmos list needs named mistakes, time per type and generated twins, none of which a fixed bank has.
proposals.needs: S10: traps. S6 or F4: per-type time from attempts.ms. The Desmos proposal, optional. S5: grid-in rejection counts. S9: looked-up words. S3: countdown and checklist. S7: Final phase hooks. Print CSS (F1).

proposals.title: Offline pack for the phone
proposals.what:
This reverses §2.14's 'no service worker'.

Where: 'Download 30 for offline' in Practice and the quick sheet, plus auto-refresh on the installed app when pref offline_pack is on.

The pack:
* The server issues a normal practice drill whose 30 items (the coach's pick, check-ins due, trap twins) come in one response with keys, rationales and reasons.
* Practice only. Never tests, contests, QOTD or challenge items; deps.access decides.
* Each trap-bearing item carries one trap-true twin, so a miss still gets its repair offline.

Caching: a small `web/sw.js` caches the session page, question.js, runner.js, ui.css, the fonts and the pack. Figures are inline SVG, so they work offline. The calculator button reads 'Needs a connection'.

Answers:
* They go through UI.saveQueue's localStorage mirror with their ms and client time.
* On reconnect they flush in order.
* The server accepts them for untimed practice.
* A banner reads 'Offline · 12 of 30 answered · syncs when you are back'.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep needs a connection for every screen. A commute becomes study time, and each pack is new questions, which a finite bank could not keep supplying without burning through itself.
proposals.needs: F5: prefetch pack (drill create returning all items). F3: saveQueue with late-accept semantics. F0/F2: sw.js registration and the manifest. S4: the session page's offline mode. F4: late answers accepted for untimed practice.

proposals.title: Paper versions for classes and tutors: every student a different test, one class report
proposals.what:
Where: 'Print N versions' (2 to 60) on any set, assignment or worksheet.

The versions: each is the same template in every slot with its own seeds (twins). Each page carries a version code (e.g. K7Q-12), a numbered answer grid and a QR code. The key booklet is by version, and each wrong option has its misconception.

Answer entry, at `/s/?c=CODE&v=K7Q-12`: the student, or the teacher for them, types answers into a 22-field grid in about a minute. Nothing else is needed.

Results: they feed the same owner results and class misconception report as online sets, e.g. '9 of 24 used the base angle as the central angle'. The report works even though every student had different numbers, because wrong answers map to named misconceptions. 'Assign a repair to these 9' follows.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep's teacher tools are hidden, assign one fixed set that students can copy, and have no paper route. A fixed bank cannot print 30 different but equal tests with keys on demand.
proposals.needs: S2: classes and assignments. F6: sets (kind 'paper' with a versions JSON). The S10/S4 worksheet print. F5: exact items via deps.access.

proposals.title: Figures and math a screen reader can use
proposals.what:
T-bank adds `Item.figure_alt`, generated from the item's params by each topic's figure builder, e.g. 'Circle with center O. Points A, G and P lie on the circle. Arc AGP is marked 108 degrees.' A build check requires every labelled point and every given measure in params to appear in the description.

Tables get real `<th>` headers and a caption.

Stems and options get spoken-math aria labels ('15 pi over 4', 'x squared minus 5').

A 'Read aloud' action (speechSynthesis, as Words' UI.speak) reads the stem and options. It is off in live tests unless the extended-time accommodation is set.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep's figures are images with no text alternative, and they float beside the text. Because we draw every figure from known numbers, each one can say exactly what it shows. That serves students with low vision and anyone studying by ear.
proposals.needs: T-bank: figure builders in satbank/topics/*/figures.py and render.py, plus the audit check. F3: workspace aria and Read aloud. S9: UI.speak. S5: the accommodation pref.
